Clinical and Psychosocial Determinants of Headache in Patients With Temporomandibular Disorders: Implications for Early Recognition and Management
items.summary: A headache is uncomfortable and functionally disruptive on its own, but when it is paired with temporomandibular disorders (TMD), which affect the temporomandibular joint (TMJ) and accompanying musculature, necessary for chewing and speaking, the combined impairment can be severe.

items.title: Columella Lengthening and Upper Lip Reconstruction in Secondary Cleft Lip Deformities Using the Abbe Flap
items.summary: In very severe bilateral cleft lip–nasal deformities, the upper lip may be extremely tight and markedly deficient in tissue, while the columella may be severely shortened, with inadequate projection.

items.title: Soft-tissue responses after bimaxillary surgery in skeletal Class III patients with and without cleft lip and palate
items.summary: This retrospective study compared postoperative soft-tissue responses to bimaxillary orthognathic surgery between skeletal Class III patients with complete unilateral cleft lip and palate (UCLP) and non-cleft patients.

items.title: Pre-tracheotomy in oral and maxillofacial surgery: proposed indications and postoperative airway outcomes
items.summary: Elective tracheotomy is frequently performed during major oral and maxillofacial surgery to prevent postoperative airway compromise; however, it is associated with significant morbidity.
items.source: British Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery

items.title: NHS expands community ear and hearing pathway across 10 ICBs
items.summary: TympaHealth-supported NHS ear and hearing pathway now live across 10 ICBs, with community pharmacies offering assessments, hearing screening and ear wax removal. Capacity up to 16,320 community appointments a year; Coventry and Warwickshire and Dorset due by early 2027.

items.title: Comment on “Accuracy of the Head and Neck Cancer Risk Calculator in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery”
items.summary: We read with interest the retrospective study by Simpson et al. [1], validating the HaNC-RC-v2 model in an OMFS cohort. The clinical problem is genuine: USOC pathways are congested with low-risk patients, and a structured triage tool that outperforms unassisted clinical judgement would have real service implications.

items.title: Risk stratification for neurosensory damage in orthognathic surgery
items.summary: Neurosensory disturbance (NSD) of the inferior alveolar nerve (IAN) is a frequent complication in bilateral sagittal split osteotomy (BSSO). This study aimed to clarify factors and stratify the risk of this complication. Consecutive patients who underwent BSSO between 2020-2023 in Santiago, Chile, were enrolled.
